-- KANBAN
--
-- The entry point: it wires the parts together and owns the view. `require` resolves against
-- this app's own source doc, so these three names are `theme.lua`, `model.lua` and
-- `ui/widgets.lua` sitting next to this file in the uploaded folder.
--
-- The split runs along one line: **anything that touches pointer state stays here.** `drag`,
-- `placement` and `col_modal` are per-viewer UI state that handlers write and the view reads,
-- so every piece that reads them (`drop_slot`, `card_of`, `column_of`) lives in this file where
-- the read and the write are visible together. `ui/widgets.lua` holds the pieces that are pure
-- functions of their arguments, and `model.lua` holds the doc.
local C = require("theme")
local W = require("ui/widgets")
local model = require("model")

local board, update = model.board, model.update
-- One shared table, not a copy: `S.drag` is written by handlers inside model.lua and read here.
-- A `local drag` on either side could not do this — a local is file-scoped, so the assignment
-- would be invisible across the boundary.
local S = model.state

-- VIEW PIECES

-- Which gap the indicator belongs in: 1 = above the first card, #list+1 = below the last.
-- A column-background drop ("into") appends, which is the trailing gap — same answer, one path.
local function drop_slot(c, list)
  if not (S.drag and S.placement) then
    return nil
  end
  if S.placement.kind == "into" then
    return S.placement.col == c.id and #list + 1 or nil
  end
  if S.placement.kind ~= "card" or S.drag.id == S.placement.id then
    return nil
  end
  for i = 1, #list do
    if list[i].id == S.placement.id then
      return S.placement.before and i or i + 1
    end
  end
end

-- `ghost` builds the floating copy: same look, but no id and no handlers, because a duplicate
-- id would register a second drag target and collide in the state store.
local function card_of(c, ghost)
  local dragging = S.drag ~= nil and S.drag.kind == "card" and S.drag.id == c.id
  local t = ui.row({
    w_full = true,
    gap = 8,
    px = 10,
    py = 9,
    radius = 8,
    fill = ghost and C.card_hi or C.card,
    stroke = { 1, ghost and C.accent or C.line_soft },
    align_center = true,
    ui.col({ grow = true, ui.text({ c.text, color = C.text, font_size = 13 }) }),
  })
  if ghost then
    return t
  end
  t.id = c.id
  t.hover_fill = C.card_hi
  t.hover_stroke = { 1, C.line }
  t.opacity = dragging and 0.3 or 1.0
  t.on_drag = function(e)
    local phase, dx, dy, scale, ox, oy = e.phase, e.dx, e.dy, e.scale, e.origin_x, e.origin_y
    update({ kind = "drag", what = "card", id = c.id, phase = phase, x = ox, y = oy, scale = scale })
  end
  t.on_drop = function(e)
    local phase, x, y = e.phase, e.x, e.y
    update({ kind = "drop", id = c.id, phase = phase, x = x, y = y })
  end
  t[#t + 1] = W.icon_button("del-card:" .. c.id, "x", function()
    update({ kind = "delete", id = c.id })
  end, C.danger)
  return t
end

local function composer(c)
  local s = ui.state("draft:" .. c.id, { text = "", open = false })
  local close = function()
    s.open = false
  end
  local send = function()
    if s.text ~= "" then
      close()
      update({ kind = "add", col = c.id })
    end
  end
  local anchor = ui.button({
    id = "add-card:" .. c.id,
    w_full = true,
    h = 32,
    radius = 6,
    center = true,
    fill = C.accent,
    hover_fill = C.accent_hi,
    press_scale = 0.97,
    ui.text({ "Add card", no_wrap = true, color = "#ffffff", font_size = 13 }),
    on_click = function()
      s.open = true
    end,
  })
  if not s.open then
    return ui.col({ px = 10, py = 10, anchor })
  end
  local panel = ui.col({
    w = 280,
    gap = 8,
    pad = 10,
    radius = 8,
    fill = C.panel,
    stroke = { 1, C.line },
    ui.input({
      value = s.text,
      id = "draft:" .. c.id,
      autofocus = true,
      w_full = true,
      h = 34,
      px = 10,
      radius = 6,
      fill = C.sunken,
      stroke = { 1, C.line },
      color = C.text,
      font_size = 13,
      on_input = function(v)
        s.text = v
      end,
      on_enter = send,
    }),
    ui.button({
      id = "submit-card:" .. c.id,
      h = 32,
      radius = 6,
      center = true,
      fill = C.accent,
      hover_fill = C.accent_hi,
      press_scale = 0.97,
      ui.text({ "Create card", no_wrap = true, color = "#ffffff", font_size = 13 }),
      on_click = send,
    }),
  })
  return ui.col({
    px = 10,
    py = 10,
    ui.overlay({ id = "composer:" .. c.id, side = "top", align = "start", on_dismiss = close, anchor, panel }),
  })
end

-- What this column is *this frame*. Mid-drag the width comes from pointer state and the doc is not
-- touched; on release the model writes it once. Same shape as the card and column drags above —
-- nothing goes to the CRDT until the gesture finishes, so a drag is one op and not sixty.
local function width_of(c)
  if S.resize and S.resize.id == c.id then
    return S.resize.w
  end
  return c.w or C.col_w
end

local function column_of(c, list)
  local body = {}
  local slot = drop_slot(c, list)
  for i = 1, #list do
    body[#body + 1] = W.guide("g:" .. c.id .. ":" .. i, slot == i)
    body[#body + 1] = card_of(list[i])
  end
  body[#body + 1] = W.guide("g:" .. c.id .. ":tail", slot == #list + 1)
  if #list == 0 then
    body[#body + 1] = W.empty_slot(slot ~= nil)
  end

  local lifting = S.drag ~= nil and S.drag.kind == "col" and S.drag.id == c.id
  return ui.col({
    id = c.id,
    w = width_of(c),
    no_shrink = true,
    -- The clamp in `actions.resize` is what the drag obeys; these are what the *layout* obeys,
    -- and they are not the same guard. A width can arrive from a peer whose theme differs, or
    -- from a doc edited by hand, and neither went past the drag.
    min_w = C.col_w_min,
    max_w = C.col_w_max,
    radius = 12,
    fill = C.panel,
    stroke = { 1, C.line_soft },
    opacity = lifting and 0.35 or 1.0,
    on_drop = function(e)
      local phase, x, y = e.phase, e.x, e.y
      update({ kind = "drop_col", col = c.id, phase = phase, x = x })
    end,
    -- header doubles as the column's drag handle
    ui.row({
      id = "colhead:" .. c.id,
      gap = 8,
      px = 12,
      py = 11,
      align_center = true,
      hover_fill = C.line_soft,
      on_drag = function(e)
        local phase, dx, dy, scale, ox, oy = e.phase, e.dx, e.dy, e.scale, e.origin_x, e.origin_y
        update({ kind = "drag", what = "col", id = c.id, phase = phase, x = ox, y = oy, scale = scale })
      end,
      ui.text({ c.name, no_wrap = true, color = C.text, font_size = 14 }),
      W.badge(#list),
      ui.col({ grow = true }),
      W.icon_button("del-col:" .. c.id, "x", function()
        update({ kind = "delete_col", id = c.id })
      end, C.danger),
    }),
    ui.col({ h = 1, w_full = true, fill = C.line_soft }),
    -- cards
    ui.col({
      id = "cards:" .. c.id,
      scroll_y = true,
      grow = true,
      px = 10,
      py = 7,
      body,
    }),
    composer(c),
  })
end

local function modal()
  local m = ui.state("col_modal", { name = "" })
  local create = function()
    update({ kind = "add_col" })
  end
  local panel = ui.col({
    id = "col-modal",
    w = 360,
    gap = 14,
    pad = 20,
    radius = 14,
    fill = C.panel,
    stroke = { 1, C.line },
    fade_in = 120,
    on_click = function() end,
    ui.text({ "New column", no_wrap = true, color = C.text, font_size = 16 }),
    ui.input({
      value = m.name,
      id = "col_name",
      autofocus = true,
      w_full = true,
      h = 36,
      px = 10,
      radius = 6,
      fill = C.sunken,
      stroke = { 1, C.line },
      color = C.text,
      font_size = 13,
      on_input = function(v)
        m.name = v
      end,
      on_enter = create,
      on_esc = function()
        update({ kind = "close_col" })
      end,
    }),
    ui.row({
      gap = 8,
      ui.col({ grow = true }),
      ui.button({
        id = "cancel-col",
        h = 34,
        px = 14,
        radius = 6,
        center = true,
        hover_fill = C.line_soft,
        press_scale = 0.97,
        ui.text({ "Cancel", no_wrap = true, color = C.muted, font_size = 13 }),
        on_click = function()
          update({ kind = "close_col" })
        end,
      }),
      ui.button({
        id = "create-col",
        h = 34,
        px = 16,
        radius = 6,
        center = true,
        fill = C.accent,
        hover_fill = C.accent_hi,
        press_scale = 0.97,
        ui.text({ "Create", no_wrap = true, color = "#ffffff", font_size = 13 }),
        on_click = create,
      }),
    }),
  })
  return ui.col({
    absolute = true,
    top = 0,
    left = 0,
    right = 0,
    bottom = 0,
    id = "col-modal-backdrop",
    center = true,
    fill = "rgba(1,4,9,0.72)",
    on_click = function()
      update({ kind = "close_col" })
    end,
    panel,
  })
end

-- ROOT
return function()
  -- Bind the mirror once per frame. `view()` repatches it before calling this, so these two
  -- are current for the whole frame — and reading them once keeps every count and index below
  -- consistent with each other.
  local columns, cards = board.columns, board.cards
  local grouped = model.by_column()
  local col_list = {}
  local flying = nil

  local col_slot = nil
  if S.drag and S.placement and S.placement.kind == "col" and S.drag.id ~= S.placement.id then
    for i = 1, #columns do
      if columns[i].id == S.placement.id then
        col_slot = S.placement.before and i or i + 1
        break
      end
    end
  end

  for i = 1, #columns do
    local c = columns[i]
    col_list[#col_list + 1] = W.guide_v("gv:" .. i, col_slot == i)
    col_list[#col_list + 1] = column_of(c, grouped[c.id])
    -- The grip is a sibling of the column, not a child of it: it has to sit in the gutter
    -- *between* two columns, and a child clipped to its parent's rounded panel would be a
    -- three-point target hanging off the edge of a corner.
    col_list[#col_list + 1] = W.grip("grip:" .. c.id, S.resize ~= nil and S.resize.id == c.id, function(phase, x, y, dx)
      update({ kind = "resize", id = c.id, phase = phase, x = x, dx = dx })
    end)
    if S.drag and S.drag.kind == "col" and S.drag.id == c.id then
      flying = ui.col({
        w = 300,
        radius = 12,
        pad = 12,
        fill = C.panel,
        stroke = { 1, C.accent },
        ui.text({ c.name, no_wrap = true, color = C.text, font_size = 14 }),
      })
    end
  end
  col_list[#col_list + 1] = W.guide_v("gv:tail", col_slot == #columns + 1)

  if S.drag and S.drag.kind == "card" then
    for i = 1, #cards do
      if cards[i].id == S.drag.id then
        flying = card_of(cards[i], true)
        break
      end
    end
  end

  -- The ghost sits at the root, outside every scroll clip, in viewport coords: `x`/`y` are
  -- `pos - grab`, i.e. where the dragged element's top-left belongs right now.
  local ghost = flying
    and ui.col({
      absolute = true,
      left = S.drag.x,
      top = S.drag.y,
      w = 300,
      scale = S.drag.scale or 1,
      opacity = 0.9,
      flying,
    })

  return ui.col({
    full = true,
    fill = C.bg,
    -- top bar
    ui.row({
      gap = 10,
      px = 24,
      py = 14,
      align_center = true,
      ui.text({ "Board", no_wrap = true, color = C.text, font_size = 18 }),
      W.badge(#cards),
      ui.col({ grow = true }),
      ui.button({
        id = "open-col",
        h = 32,
        px = 14,
        radius = 8,
        center = true,
        fill = C.accent,
        hover_fill = C.accent_hi,
        press_scale = 0.97,
        ui.text({ "+  Column", no_wrap = true, color = "#ffffff", font_size = 13 }),
        on_click = function()
          update({ kind = "open_col" })
        end,
      }),
    }),
    ui.col({ h = 1, w_full = true, fill = C.line_soft }),
    -- board
    ui.col({
      id = "board_zoom",
      zoomable = true,
      grow = true,
      w_full = true,
      fill = C.bg,
      ui.row({
        id = "board",
        h_full = true,
        stretch = true,
        px = 13,
        py = 20,
        col_list,
      }),
    }),
    ghost or false,
    S.col_modal and modal(),
  })
end

-- MODEL
--
-- Columns and cards live in the CRDT, not in Lua tables: `board.columns` and `board.cards` are
-- the mirror, refreshed from Loro before every frame, and every mutation goes back through the
-- doc. That is what makes the board survive a restart, and what will make a second peer's drag
-- show up here.
--
-- One rule to keep in mind while reading the actions below: **the mirror is a frame behind your
-- own write.** `:set` and friends go straight to Loro, and `board.cards` is only repatched in
-- view(). So read what you need first, then write; never read back what you just wrote.
--
-- This module runs once per app instance -- `require` caches it -- so the seeding below happens
-- once no matter how many files ask for the model.
local C = require("theme")

local board = doc:open("board")

-- Module scope runs on every open, so seeding has to be guarded or reopening the app would
-- wipe the board it just loaded.
--
-- `w` is seeded so the field is there to read, but every reader still says `c.w or C.col_w`:
-- boards created before columns had a width are the common case, not the exotic one.
if not board.columns then
  board:set({ "columns" }, doc.list({
    doc.map({ id = "c-todo", name = "Todo", w = C.col_w }),
    doc.map({ id = "c-doing", name = "In Progress", w = C.col_w }),
    doc.map({ id = "c-done", name = "Done", w = C.col_w }),
  }))
end
if not board.cards then
  board:set({ "cards" }, doc.list({
    doc.map({ id = "k1", col = "c-todo", text = "Wire the MCP bridge" }),
    doc.map({ id = "k2", col = "c-todo", text = "Font weight in TextSpec" }),
    doc.map({ id = "k3", col = "c-doing", text = "Error boundaries in walk" }),
    doc.map({ id = "k4", col = "c-done", text = "ui.state + sweep" }),
  }))
end

-- Per-viewer pointer state -- what *this* pointer is doing right now. Deliberately not in the
-- doc: broadcasting a half-finished drag would show everyone else your mouse.
--
-- It has to be a table field rather than a local now that the view lives in another file. A
-- `local drag` is file-scoped, and reassigning it here could never be seen from main.lua; a
-- field on an exported table can. That is the whole cost of the split, and it is why there is
-- exactly one of these tables rather than one per module.
local S = { drag = nil, placement = nil, col_modal = false, resize = nil }

local actions = {}

local function index_of(list, id)
  for i = 1, #list do
    if list[i].id == id then
      return i
    end
  end
end

local function find(list, id)
  local i = index_of(list, id)
  return i and list[i]
end

-- Loro's move removes then reinserts, so `to` is the index the element ends up at *after* its
-- own removal. Dragging downwards therefore lands one slot short unless the target is nudged.
local function target_index(list, from, anchor_id, before)
  local at = index_of(list, anchor_id)
  if not at then
    return #list
  end
  local to = before and at or at + 1
  if from < to then
    to = to - 1
  end
  return to
end

local function commit_card()
  local cards = board.cards
  local from = index_of(cards, S.drag.id)
  if not from then
    return
  end
  -- Dropped on a column rather than on a card: leave the ordering alone and just restamp the
  -- column. The card list is flat, so `col` is the only thing that has to change.
  if S.placement.kind == "into" then
    board:set({ "cards", S.drag.id, "col" }, S.placement.col)
    return
  end
  if S.drag.id == S.placement.id then
    return
  end
  local at = index_of(cards, S.placement.id)
  local anchor = at and cards[at]
  -- Move first, then restamp: :move retargets the element's `pos` register and :set writes a
  -- field inside it, and those are independent registers. Deleting and reinserting would mint
  -- a new element, which is how a concurrent edit turns into a duplicated card.
  board:move({ "cards", S.drag.id }, target_index(cards, from, S.placement.id, S.placement.before))
  if anchor and anchor.col ~= cards[from].col then
    board:set({ "cards", S.drag.id, "col" }, anchor.col)
  end
end

local function commit_col()
  if S.drag.id == S.placement.id then
    return
  end
  local columns = board.columns
  local from = index_of(columns, S.drag.id)
  if not from then
    return
  end
  board:move(
    { "columns", S.drag.id },
    target_index(columns, from, S.placement.id, S.placement.before)
  )
end

local function commit()
  if not (S.drag and S.placement) then
    return
  end
  if S.drag.kind == "col" then
    commit_col()
  else
    commit_card()
  end
end

function actions.add(msg)
  local s = ui.state("draft:" .. msg.col)
  if s.text and s.text ~= "" then
    board:insert({ "cards" }, doc.map({ id = uuid(), col = msg.col, text = s.text }))
    s.text = ""
  end
end

function actions.delete(msg)
  board:delete({ "cards", msg.id })
end

function actions.drag(msg)
  if msg.phase == "start" then
    S.drag = { kind = msg.what, id = msg.id, x = msg.x, y = msg.y, scale = msg.scale }
  elseif msg.phase == "move" then
    if S.drag then
      S.drag.x, S.drag.y, S.drag.scale = msg.x, msg.y, msg.scale
    end
    S.placement = nil
  elseif msg.phase == "end" then
    S.drag, S.placement = nil, nil
  end
end

function actions.drop(msg)
  if not (S.drag and S.drag.kind == "card") then
    return
  end
  if msg.phase == "over" then
    S.placement = { kind = "card", id = msg.id, before = msg.y < 0.5 }
  else
    commit()
  end
end

-- One target, two meanings: a card lands *inside* the column, a column lands *beside* it.
function actions.drop_col(msg)
  if not S.drag then
    return
  end
  if msg.phase == "over" then
    if S.drag.kind == "col" then
      S.placement = { kind = "col", id = msg.col, before = msg.x < 0.5 }
    else
      S.placement = { kind = "into", col = msg.col }
    end
  else
    commit()
  end
end

-- Column width goes in the doc, and the two things it is *not* are worth saying out loud.
--
-- Not source. The obvious home for a size is the `ui.col` that draws the column — that is what
-- docs/design/code-as-tree.md §11 is about — but there is no such node: `column_of` is one
-- constructor drawing every column, so main.lua has nothing in it that means "the Todo column".
-- That is nid-channel.md §5's instance-identity limit, met the first time it mattered.
--
-- Not per-viewer state either, which is the other tempting answer. A wide column is a claim about
-- the work in it, so it belongs to the board the way the column's name does — the next person to
-- open this should see the board somebody arranged, not their own default.
--
-- The clamp runs on every move rather than once at the end, or the pointer walks past the limit
-- and the column sits still until it comes all the way back.
function actions.resize(msg)
  if msg.phase == "start" then
    local c = find(board.columns, msg.id)
    local w = c and c.w or C.col_w
    S.resize = { id = msg.id, from = w, w = w }
    return
  end
  if not (S.resize and S.resize.id == msg.id) then
    return
  end
  if msg.phase == "move" then
    local w = S.resize.from + msg.dx
    S.resize.w = math.max(C.col_w_min, math.min(C.col_w_max, w))
  else
    -- Written unconditionally, including when the press never moved. A guard here looked
    -- obviously right and turned out to be theatre: Loro's own `insert` skips an op whose
    -- value already matches, and `app_host`'s `:set` adds no check of its own, so an
    -- unchanged width never reaches the history either way. Removing the guard fails no test,
    -- which is how it was found. `a_resize_that_never_moved_writes_nothing` pins the behaviour
    -- we are leaning on, so this comment stops being true loudly rather than quietly.
    board:set({ "columns", msg.id, "w" }, S.resize.w)
    S.resize = nil
  end
end

function actions.open_col()
  S.col_modal = true
end

function actions.close_col()
  S.col_modal = false
  -- Clear the draft too, or the next open shows the abandoned text.
  ui.state("col_modal", { name = "" }).name = ""
end

function actions.add_col()
  local m = ui.state("col_modal")
  if not m.name or m.name == "" then
    return
  end
  board:insert({ "columns" }, doc.map({ id = uuid(), name = m.name, w = C.col_w }))
  m.name = ""
  S.col_modal = false
end

function actions.delete_col(msg)
  -- Collect first, delete second. Each :delete lands in the doc immediately but the mirror is
  -- only repatched in view(), so iterating `board.cards` while deleting from it would be
  -- walking a stale list.
  local doomed = {}
  for _, c in ipairs(board.cards) do
    if c.col == msg.id then
      doomed[#doomed + 1] = c.id
    end
  end
  for _, id in ipairs(doomed) do
    board:delete({ "cards", id })
  end
  board:delete({ "columns", msg.id })
end

local function update(msg)
  local f = actions[msg.kind]
  if not f then
    print("unknown action:", msg.kind)
    return
  end
  f(msg)
end

-- Cards keyed by the column they sit in. A derivation over the mirror, so it is recomputed every
-- frame rather than cached: the tables it reads are repatched under it.
local function by_column()
  local out = {}
  for _, c in ipairs(board.columns) do
    out[c.id] = {}
  end
  for _, card in ipairs(board.cards) do
    local list = out[card.col]
    if list then
      list[#list + 1] = card
    end
  end
  return out
end

return {
  board = board,
  state = S,
  update = update,
  by_column = by_column,
}

-- Small pieces that draw and nothing else.
--
-- The boundary here is not "small" but *pure*: every function below is a function of its
-- arguments and the palette. None of them touch the board, the pointer state or `update`, which
-- is what lets them sit in another file without anything being passed down to reach them.
local C = require("theme")

local M = {}

-- Guides are rendered on *every* gap, always, so the space is permanently reserved and nothing
-- shifts when a drop target appears — only the line's alpha changes. `fade` is keyed by id:
-- that's where the runtime parks the tween, so retargeting mid-flight reverses smoothly.
function M.guide(id, on)
  return ui.col({
    py = 3,
    w_full = true,
    ui.col({ id = id, h = 2, radius = 1, fill = C.accent, fade = { on and 1 or 0, 140 } }),
  })
end

-- Vertical twin, for column reordering. No height: the board row is `stretch`, so it fills.
function M.guide_v(id, on)
  return ui.col({
    px = 7,
    ui.col({
      id = id,
      w = 2,
      grow = true,
      radius = 1,
      fill = C.accent,
      fade = { on and 1 or 0, 140 },
    }),
  })
end

-- The resize grip: a hairline in the gutter to the right of a column. Same shape as `guide_v` on
-- purpose — it stands in the same kind of gap and must not push the columns around by being there.
--
-- Faint but never invisible. `guide_v` can fade to nothing because a drop target announces itself
-- when it becomes relevant; a grip has to be found before it is useful, and a control you can only
-- hit by guessing where it is is not a control. Hover brightens it, dragging holds it bright.
--
-- Pure like everything else here: it is handed the handler rather than reaching for `update`.
function M.grip(id, active, on_drag)
  return ui.col({
    px = 4,
    ui.col({
      id = id,
      w = 3,
      grow = true,
      radius = 2,
      fill = active and C.accent or C.line,
      hover_fill = C.accent,
      on_drag = on_drag,
    }),
  })
end

-- Both of these sit on the *main* axis of a row next to text that can be any length — the badge
-- beside a column name, the button beside a card's body. A flex item shrinks to its min-content
-- width before its neighbour gives way, so without `no_shrink` a long card title squashes the
-- delete button until its glyph wraps, and the control the user is reaching for is the one that
-- disappears. Grows nothing, costs nothing, and only matters when space runs out.
function M.badge(n)
  return ui.row({
    px = 7,
    py = 1,
    radius = 10,
    fill = C.line_soft,
    center = true,
    no_shrink = true,
    ui.text({ tostring(n), no_wrap = true, color = C.muted, font_size = 11 }),
  })
end

function M.icon_button(id, glyph, on_press, hover)
  return ui.button({
    id = id,
    w = 22,
    h = 22,
    radius = 6,
    center = true,
    no_shrink = true,
    hover_fill = hover or C.line,
    press_scale = 0.92,
    ui.text({ glyph, no_wrap = true, color = C.muted, font_size = 13 }),
    on_click = on_press,
  })
end

function M.empty_slot(on)
  return ui.col({
    h = 64,
    center = true,
    radius = 8,
    stroke = { 1, on and C.accent or C.line_soft },
    ui.text({ "drop a card here", no_wrap = true, color = on and C.accent or C.muted, font_size = 12 }),
  })
end

return M

-- MODEL
--
-- `chat` holds the channel list; each channel's messages live in their own doc,
-- `channel/<id>`, so one busy channel never makes another's doc large. Search spans them all
-- because `index.lua` matches `channel/*`.
local M = { S = { channel = "general", editing = nil } }

local chat = doc:open("chat")
if not chat.channels then
  chat:set({ "channels" }, doc.list({
    doc.map({ id = "general", name = "general" }),
    doc.map({ id = "design", name = "design" }),
  }))
end
M.chat = chat

local docs = {}
function M.channel(cid)
  local d = docs[cid]
  if not d then
    d = doc:open("channel/" .. cid)
    docs[cid] = d
  end
  return d
end

-- Seeded so a fresh app (and the app-shipped tests' empty tab) has something to find.
local general = M.channel("general")
if not general.messages then
  general:set({ "messages" }, doc.list({
    doc.map({ id = "seed-1", author = "anu", text = "the deploy is green", sent_at = 1 }),
    doc.map({ id = "seed-2", author = "abe", text = "lunch at noon?", sent_at = 2 }),
  }))
end

local function message(text)
  return doc.map({ id = uuid(), author = "me", text = text, sent_at = now() })
end

-- Read the mirror before writing: `d.messages` is a frame behind, and only decides whether the
-- list exists yet.
function M.send(text)
  if text == "" then
    return
  end
  local S, d = M.S, M.channel(M.S.channel)
  if S.editing then
    d:set({ "messages", S.editing, "text" }, text)
    S.editing = nil
  elseif d.messages then
    d:insert({ "messages" }, message(text))
  else
    d:set({ "messages" }, doc.list({ message(text) }))
  end
end

function M.delete(id)
  M.channel(M.S.channel):delete({ "messages", id })
  if M.S.editing == id then
    M.S.editing = nil
  end
end

-- "channel/design" → "design"
function M.channel_of(doc_name)
  return doc_name:match("^channel/(.+)$")
end

return M

local C = require("theme")
local M = require("model")
local Stage = require("stage")
local Inspector = require("inspector")
local Handles = require("handles")

local selected = nil -- the selected part's id
local built = { key = nil, frame = nil } -- the canvas visual; rebuilt on a new selection or edit
local play = nil -- { name, drawing, clip } while a clip plays on the canvas; nil is edit mode
local seen_at = 1 -- the viewport's zoom, so selection marks keep their screen size
-- While a point dot is held: its shape `i`, the points moving (`{ j, k, from }`, the held one
-- first), and `d`, how far they have moved, in drawing units. While a part is held: `ids`, the
-- set of parts moving with it, and `d`.
local drag = nil

-- The canvas draws the asset scaled up by building a scaled copy, rather than scaling the
-- element: hits keep reporting part ids, and canvas units are drawing units times the zoom.
local function scaled_path(path, z)
  local out = {}
  for i, cmd in ipairs(path) do
    local c = { cmd[1] }
    for j = 2, #cmd do
      c[j] = cmd[j] * z
    end
    out[i] = c
  end
  return out
end

-- A colour stays as it is; a gradient's points and radii are in drawing space, so they scale
-- too. Angles and stops don't.
local function scaled_fill(fill, z)
  if type(fill) ~= "table" then
    return fill
  end
  local function pt(p)
    return p and { p[1] * z, p[2] * z }
  end
  local kind, g = next(fill)
  local out = { stops = g.stops, extend = g.extend }
  if kind == "linear" then
    out.from, out.to = pt(g.from), pt(g.to)
  elseif kind == "radial" then
    out.center, out.focus = pt(g.center), pt(g.focus)
    out.radius, out.focus_radius = g.radius * z, g.focus_radius and g.focus_radius * z
  else -- sweep
    out.center, out.from_angle, out.to_angle = pt(g.center), g.from_angle, g.to_angle
  end
  return { [kind] = out }
end

-- A lone length may be a var, `"@line"`: it stays a name here, and the vars scale instead.
local function len(v, z)
  return type(v) == "number" and v * z or v
end

local function scaled_shape(s, z)
  if s.shadow then
    local sh, r = s.shadow, s.shadow.rect
    local rect = { r[1] * z, r[2] * z, r[3] * z, r[4] * z }
    local radius = len(sh.radius or 0, z)
    return { shadow = { rect = rect, radius = radius, blur = len(sh.blur, z), color = sh.color } }
  end
  local stroke = s.stroke and { len(s.stroke[1], z), s.stroke[2] }
  return { path = scaled_path(s.path, z), fill = scaled_fill(s.fill, z), stroke = stroke }
end

-- The asset at canvas scale, with the `outline` part's outlines drawn again in the accent colour
-- and its path points on top as dots.
local function canvas_drawing(parts, z, outline)
  local out, held = {}, nil
  for i, p in ipairs(parts) do
    local shapes = {}
    for _, s in ipairs(p.shapes or {}) do
      table.insert(shapes, scaled_shape(s, z))
    end
    if p.id == outline then
      for _, s in ipairs(p.shapes or {}) do
        if s.path then -- a shadow has no outline to trace
          table.insert(shapes, { path = scaled_path(s.path, z), stroke = { 3 / seen_at, C.accent } })
        end
      end
    end
    out[i] = {
      id = p.id,
      parent = p.parent,
      pivot = { p.pivot[1] * z, p.pivot[2] * z },
      shapes = #shapes > 0 and shapes or nil,
    }
    if p.id == outline then
      held = p
    end
  end
  for _, h in ipairs(held and Handles.parts(held, z, seen_at) or {}) do
    table.insert(out, h)
  end
  local size = M.asset.size
  local vars = {} -- a number var is always a length
  for name, v in pairs(M.asset.vars or {}) do
    vars[name] = len(v, z)
  end
  return gfx.drawing({ size = { size[1] * z, size[2] * z }, vars = vars, parts = out })
end

local DIVS = { 1, 2, 4, 10, 20 } -- snap steps as divisions of a unit: 1/20 stays exact, 0.05 not

-- `v` on the finest step still a few pixels apart on screen: whole units at a glance, twentieths
-- up close.
local function snap(v)
  local div = 1
  for _, d in ipairs(DIVS) do
    if C.zoom * seen_at / d >= 4 then
      div = d
    end
  end
  return math.floor(v * div + 0.5) / div
end

-- `parts` with the held points where the drag has them, copying only what that changes.
local function dragged(parts)
  local out = table.clone(parts)
  for n, p in ipairs(parts) do
    if drag.ids then
      out[n] = drag.ids[p.id] and M.moved(p, drag.d) or p
    elseif p.id == selected then
      local part, shape = table.clone(p), table.clone(p.shapes[drag.i])
      shape.path = table.clone(shape.path)
      for _, m in ipairs(drag.moves) do -- an end and its control can share a command
        shape.path[m.j] = table.clone(shape.path[m.j])
      end
      for _, m in ipairs(drag.moves) do
        shape.path[m.j][2 * m.k] = m.from[1] + drag.d[1]
        shape.path[m.j][2 * m.k + 1] = m.from[2] + drag.d[2]
      end
      part.shapes = table.clone(p.shapes)
      part.shapes[drag.i] = shape
      out[n] = part
    end
  end
  return out
end

local function key(...)
  return { "views", M.view, "parts", ... }
end

-- Writes the held parts where the drag left them, and the sockets riding them. Paths go whole.
local function write_moved(parts)
  local d = drag.d
  for _, p in ipairs(parts) do
    if drag.ids[p.id] then
      local m = M.moved(p, d)
      M.asset:set(key(p.id, "pivot"), M.tag(m.pivot))
      for i, s in ipairs(m.shapes) do
        if s.path then
          M.asset:set(key(p.id, "shapes", i, "path"), M.tag(s.path))
        end
        if type(s.fill) == "table" then
          M.asset:set(key(p.id, "shapes", i, "fill"), M.tag(s.fill))
        end
        if s.shadow then
          M.asset:set(key(p.id, "shapes", i, "shadow", "rect"), M.tag(s.shadow.rect))
        end
      end
    end
  end
  for name, s in pairs(M.asset.sockets or {}) do
    if drag.ids[s.part] then
      M.asset:set({ "sockets", name, "at" }, M.tag({ s.at[1] + d[1], s.at[2] + d[2] }))
    end
  end
end

local function visual(parts)
  local live = drag and drag.d[1] .. "," .. drag.d[2] or ""
  local key = table.concat({ M.name, selected or "", Inspector.rev, seen_at, live }, ":")
  if built.key ~= key then
    built.key = key
    built.frame = canvas_drawing(drag and dragged(parts) or parts, C.zoom, selected):pose({})
  end
  return built.frame
end

-- A clip at canvas scale: moves are in drawing units, so x and y scale; turns and scales don't.
local function scaled_clip(clip, z)
  local tracks = {}
  for part, props in pairs(clip.tracks) do
    tracks[part] = {}
    for prop, keys in pairs(props) do
      local k = (prop == "x" or prop == "y") and z or 1
      local out = {}
      for i, key in ipairs(keys) do
        out[i] = { key[1], key[2] * k, key[3] }
      end
      tracks[part][prop] = out
    end
  end
  return { length = clip.length, loop = clip.loop, tracks = tracks }
end

-- Every press makes a new clip handle, which is what restarts a clip that is already playing.
local function start(name)
  play = {
    name = name,
    drawing = canvas_drawing(M.parts(), C.zoom, nil),
    clip = gfx.clip(scaled_clip(M.asset.clips[name], C.zoom)),
  }
end

local function chip(id, label, on, on_click)
  return ui.button({
    id = id,
    px = 10,
    py = 6,
    radius = 6,
    fill = on and C.row_selected or C.panel,
    hover_fill = on and C.row_selected or C.row_hover,
    on_click = on_click,
    ui.text({ label, color = on and C.accent or C.text, font_size = 13, no_wrap = true }),
  })
end

local function asset_tab(name)
  return chip("asset:" .. name, name, name == M.name, function()
    selected, play = nil, nil
    M.open(name)
  end)
end

-- "edit" shows the rest pose and selects parts; a clip name plays that clip in a world.
local function clip_bar()
  local names = {}
  for name in pairs(M.asset.clips or {}) do
    table.insert(names, name)
  end
  table.sort(names)
  local chips = { chip("mode:edit", "edit", play == nil, function()
    play = nil
  end) }
  for _, name in ipairs(names) do
    local on = play ~= nil and play.name == name
    table.insert(chips, chip("clip:" .. name, name, on, function()
      start(name)
    end))
  end
  return ui.row({ gap = 6, wrap = true, chips })
end

-- Edit mode is a frame, so a click names the part; play mode is a world, whose clicks would
-- only name the whole asset — hence two modes rather than one.
local function canvas(parts)
  if play then
    local size = M.asset.size
    return ui.world({
      id = "stage",
      width = size[1] * C.zoom,
      height = size[2] * C.zoom,
      { id = M.name, pos = { 0, 0 }, drawing = play.drawing, clip = play.clip },
    })
  end
  return ui.frame({
    id = "canvas",
    visual = visual(parts),
    -- A click on no part clears the selection; one on a point dot keeps it.
    on_click = function(e)
      if not (e.shape and e.shape:sub(1, 3) == "pt:") then
        selected = e.shape
      end
    end,
    -- A held dot or part follows the pointer on the canvas alone; letting go writes it. A
    -- part takes the parts under it along. A drag from empty canvas pans.
    drag_on_shapes = true,
    on_drag = function(e)
      if e.phase == "start" then
        if e.shape and e.shape:sub(1, 3) ~= "pt:" then
          selected = e.shape
          drag = { ids = M.family(parts, e.shape), d = { 0, 0 }, x0 = e.x, y0 = e.y }
        end
        local i, j, k = (e.shape or ""):match("^pt:(%d+):(%d+):(%d+)$")
        for _, p in ipairs(i and parts or {}) do
          if p.id == selected then
            i, j, k = tonumber(i), tonumber(j), tonumber(k)
            local path = p.shapes[i].path
            local moves = { { j = j, k = k } }
            for _, r in ipairs(Handles.riders(path, j, k)) do
              table.insert(moves, r)
            end
            for _, m in ipairs(moves) do
              m.from = { path[m.j][2 * m.k], path[m.j][2 * m.k + 1] }
            end
            drag = { i = i, moves = moves, d = { 0, 0 }, x0 = e.x, y0 = e.y }
          end
        end
      elseif drag then
        -- A held point snaps, and the rest move by what it moved; a part moves by snapped steps.
        local dx, dy = (e.x - drag.x0) / C.zoom, (e.y - drag.y0) / C.zoom
        if drag.ids then
          drag.d = { snap(dx), snap(dy) }
        else
          local from = drag.moves[1].from
          drag.d = { snap(from[1] + dx) - from[1], snap(from[2] + dy) - from[2] }
        end
        if e.phase == "end" then
          if drag.ids then
            write_moved(parts)
          end
          for _, m in ipairs(drag.moves or {}) do
            local cmd = { "views", M.view, "parts", selected, "shapes", drag.i, "path", m.j }
            local px, py = table.clone(cmd), table.clone(cmd)
            table.insert(px, 2 * m.k)
            table.insert(py, 2 * m.k + 1)
            M.asset:set(px, m.from[1] + drag.d[1])
            M.asset:set(py, m.from[2] + drag.d[2])
          end
          drag = nil
          Inspector.rev += 1 -- the canvas rebuilds from the mirror, which has it by then
        end
      end
    end,
  })
end

local function part_row(p)
  local on = p.id == selected
  return ui.button({
    id = "part:" .. p.id,
    px = 12,
    py = 8,
    gap = 8,
    align_center = true,

-- The open asset: a workspace doc holding a drawing (its views and clips) or a stage (a scene of
-- placed assets). An asset is seeded from its bundled seed; after that the asset is the truth.
local M = {}

M.view = "front"

-- Each seed gives the asset's roots; a drawing's `parts` go under `views`.
M.seeds = {
  hero = function()
    local hero = require("seed/hero")
    return {
      size = hero.size,
      vars = hero.vars,
      parts = hero.parts,
      clips = require("seed/clips"),
      sockets = { head_top = { kind = "hat", part = "head", at = { 80, 34 }, width = 60 } },
      -- Top-down, only the feet meet a wall: a small circle where they stand.
      world = { collider = { circle = 16, at = { 80, 222 } } },
    }
  end,
  toggle = function()
    return require("seed/toggle")
  end,
  chest = function()
    return require("seed/chest")
  end,
  hat = function()
    return require("seed/hat")
  end,
  crate = function()
    return require("seed/crate")
  end,
  room = function()
    return require("seed/room")
  end,
}
M.names = { "hero", "toggle", "chest", "hat", "crate" }
M.scenes = { room = true }

-- Doc writes are tagged at every depth: a table with only positional entries is a list,
-- anything else a map.
local function tag(v)
  if type(v) ~= "table" then
    return v
  end
  local out, n = {}, 0
  for k, x in pairs(v) do
    out[k] = tag(x)
    n += 1
  end
  return (n > 0 and n == #v) and doc.list(out) or doc.map(out)
end
M.tag = tag

-- Part `id` and every part under it, as a set: a moved arm takes its hand along.
function M.family(parts, id)
  local ids, grew = { [id] = true }, true
  while grew do -- a child may be listed before its parent
    grew = false
    for _, p in ipairs(parts) do
      if p.parent and ids[p.parent] and not ids[p.id] then
        ids[p.id], grew = true, true
      end
    end
  end
  return ids
end

local function shift(p, d)
  return p and { p[1] + d[1], p[2] + d[2] }
end

-- A copy of `part` moved by `d`: its pivot and every point it draws in drawing space — path
-- points, gradient points, a shadow's corner. Lengths, angles and stops stay.
function M.moved(part, d)
  local out = table.clone(part)
  out.pivot = shift(part.pivot, d)
  out.shapes = {}
  for i, s in ipairs(part.shapes or {}) do
    local c = table.clone(s)
    if s.shadow then
      local r = s.shadow.rect
      c.shadow = table.clone(s.shadow)
      c.shadow.rect = { r[1] + d[1], r[2] + d[2], r[3], r[4] }
    end
    if s.path then
      c.path = {}
      for j, cmd in ipairs(s.path) do
        local m = { cmd[1] }
        for k = 2, #cmd do -- x, y, x, y…
          m[k] = cmd[k] + d[1 + k % 2]
        end
        c.path[j] = m
      end
    end
    if type(s.fill) == "table" then
      local kind, g = next(s.fill)
      local f = table.clone(g)
      f.from, f.to = shift(g.from, d), shift(g.to, d)
      f.center, f.focus = shift(g.center, d), shift(g.focus, d)
      c.fill = { [kind] = f }
    end
    out.shapes[i] = c
  end
  return out
end

local loaded = {}

-- An asset by name, writing any root its seed has and it lacks — so a seed that grows (the
-- hero's socket) reaches an asset made before it. What it writes shows from the next frame.
function M.load(name)
  if loaded[name] then
    return loaded[name]
  end
  local a = asset:open(name)
  for k, v in pairs(M.seeds[name] and M.seeds[name]() or {}) do
    local root, value = k, v
    if k == "parts" then
      root, value = "views", { [M.view] = { parts = v } }
    end
    if a[root] == nil then
      a:set({ root }, tag(value))
    end
  end
  loaded[name] = a
  return a
end

function M.open(name)
  M.name = name
  M.asset = M.load(name)
end

-- The current view's parts of a drawing asset, or nil before its seed is visible.
function M.parts(a)
  local views = (a or M.asset).views
  return views and views[M.view] and views[M.view].parts
end

M.open("hero")

return M

-- Stage edit: every entity of a scene drawn as a named instance in one frame, so a drag reports
-- the entity it grabbed. A drag moves it live; one write lands on release.
local C = require("theme")
local M = require("model")

local S = {}
local rests = {} -- asset name → { frame = its rest pose, asset = its mirror }, built once
local drag = nil -- { id, x0, y0, from, at, released } while an entity is moved
local floor = nil -- the stage's backdrop, built on first use
local play = nil -- { name, clips = { entity id → clip handle } } while a stage plays; nil is edit

local function rest(name)
  if not rests[name] then
    local a = M.load(name)
    local parts = M.parts(a)
    if not parts then
      return nil -- seeded this frame; it shows from the next
    end
    local drawing = gfx.drawing({ size = a.size, vars = a.vars, parts = parts })
    rests[name] = { frame = drawing:pose({}), drawing = drawing, asset = a }
  end
  return rests[name]
end

local variants = {} -- entity id → its look when it sets `vars`, rebuilt when they change

-- An entity's look: its asset's rest, or — when the entity sets `vars` — a variant of it.
local function look(e)
  local r = rest(e.asset)
  if not r or not e.vars then
    return r
  end
  local said = {}
  for name, v in pairs(e.vars) do
    table.insert(said, name .. "=" .. tostring(v))
  end
  table.sort(said)
  local key = e.asset .. ":" .. table.concat(said, ",")
  if not variants[e.id] or variants[e.id].key ~= key then
    local a = r.asset
    local module = { size = a.size, vars = a.vars, parts = M.parts(a) }
    local drawing = gfx.drawing(module, { vars = e.vars })
    variants[e.id] = { key = key, drawing = drawing, frame = drawing:pose({}), asset = a }
  end
  return variants[e.id]
end

local SNAP = 24 -- how near a plug must come to a matching socket to equip there
local last = {} -- last view's placements: where a grab starts, where sockets are while dragging

-- Where each entity's box goes: a drag in flight, its own position, or — mounted — its host's
-- socket less its own plug. A released drag is dropped here: this view's mirror already has it.
local function placements(entities)
  if drag and drag.released then
    drag = nil
  end
  local at, by_id = {}, {}
  for _, e in ipairs(entities) do
    by_id[e.id] = e
  end
  local function place(e)
    if at[e.id] ~= nil then
      return at[e.id] or nil
    end
    at[e.id] = false -- a mount cycle ends here instead of recursing forever
    if drag and drag.id == e.id then
      at[e.id] = drag.snap and drag.snap.at or drag.at
    elseif e.pos then
      at[e.id] = { e.pos[1], e.pos[2] }
    elseif e.mount and by_id[e.mount.to] then
      local host, mine = rest(by_id[e.mount.to].asset), rest(e.asset)
      local socket = host and host.asset.sockets and host.asset.sockets[e.mount.socket]
      local plug = mine and mine.asset.plug
      local h = place(by_id[e.mount.to])
      if socket and plug and h then
        at[e.id] = { h[1] + socket.at[1] - plug.at[1], h[2] + socket.at[2] - plug.at[2] }
      end
    end
    return at[e.id] or nil
  end
  for _, e in ipairs(entities) do
    place(e)
  end
  return at
end

local function backdrop(w, h)
  if not floor then
    local rect = gfx.path({
      { "move", 0, 0 }, { "line", w, 0 }, { "line", w, h }, { "line", 0, h }, { "close" },
    })
    floor = gfx.fill({ path = rect, brush = gfx.solid(C.floor) })
  end
  return floor
end

-- Every socket the dragged entity's plug fits, as stage points — the interface is the kind.
-- An entity mounted on the dragged one can't be its host: that would be a cycle.
local function sockets_for(ent, entities)
  local plug = rest(ent.asset) and rest(ent.asset).asset.plug
  local found = {}
  for _, host in ipairs(entities) do
    local r, h = rest(host.asset), last[host.id]
    local riding = host.mount and host.mount.to == ent.id
    if plug and r and h and host.id ~= ent.id and not riding then
      for name, socket in pairs(r.asset.sockets or {}) do
        if socket.kind == plug.kind then
          local x, y = h[1] + socket.at[1], h[2] + socket.at[2]
          table.insert(found, { to = host.id, socket = name, x = x, y = y })
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return found, plug
end

local function on_drag(e, entities)
  if e.phase == "start" then
    for _, ent in ipairs(entities) do
      if ent.id == e.shape and last[ent.id] then
        local from = { last[ent.id][1], last[ent.id][2] }
        local sockets, plug = sockets_for(ent, entities)
        drag = { id = ent.id, ent = ent, x0 = e.x, y0 = e.y, from = from, at = from }
        drag.sockets, drag.plug = sockets, plug
      end
    end
  elseif drag and not drag.released then
    drag.at = { drag.from[1] + e.x - drag.x0, drag.from[2] + e.y - drag.y0 }
    drag.snap = nil
    for _, s in ipairs(drag.sockets) do
      local px, py = drag.at[1] + drag.plug.at[1], drag.at[2] + drag.plug.at[2]
      if (px - s.x) ^ 2 + (py - s.y) ^ 2 <= SNAP * SNAP then
        local at = { s.x - drag.plug.at[1], s.y - drag.plug.at[2] }
        drag.snap = { to = s.to, socket = s.socket, at = at }
      end
    end
    if e.phase == "end" then
      local function field(name)
        return { "scene", "entities", drag.id, name }
      end
      local ent, snap = drag.ent, drag.snap
      if snap then -- equip: it rides the socket and has no place of its own
        M.asset:set(field("mount"), doc.map({ to = snap.to, socket = snap.socket }))
        if ent.pos then
          M.asset:delete(field("pos"))
        end
      else
        M.asset:set(field("pos"), doc.list({ drag.at[1], drag.at[2] }))
        if ent.mount then -- pulled off its socket
          M.asset:delete(field("mount"))
        end
      end
      drag.released = true
    end
  end
end

local function ring(x, y, r)
  local k = 0.5523 * r
  return gfx.path({
    { "move", x + r, y }, { "cubic", x + r, y + k, x + k, y + r, x, y + r },
    { "cubic", x - k, y + r, x - r, y + k, x - r, y },
    { "cubic", x - r, y - k, x - k, y - r, x, y - r },
    { "cubic", x + k, y - r, x + r, y - k, x + r, y }, { "close" },
  })
end

-- The world fields an entity plays with: its asset's `world` defaults, each replaced whole by
-- the entity's own, where `false` takes one away. Keys are the room's: only an entity has them.
local FIELDS = { "collider", "sensor", "loose", "group", "blocks" }
function S.fields(e, a)
  local out = { controller = e.controller or nil }
  for _, k in ipairs(FIELDS) do
    local v = e[k]
    if v == nil then
      v = a.world and a.world[k]
    end
    out[k] = v or nil
  end
  return out
end

-- Each collider as a line and each sensor dashed, where the entity stands. A mounted entity
-- has neither while it rides.
local function body_marks(entities)
  local marks = {}
  for _, e in ipairs(entities) do
    local r, p = rest(e.asset), last[e.id]
    local f = r and p and not e.mount and S.fields(e, r.asset) or {}
    for _, k in ipairs({ "collider", "sensor" }) do
      local s = f[k]
      if s then
        local at = s.at or { 0, 0 }
        local x, y = p[1] + at[1], p[2] + at[2]
        local path = s.rect and gfx.path({
          { "move", x, y }, { "line", x + s.rect[1], y }, { "line", x + s.rect[1], y + s.rect[2] },
          { "line", x, y + s.rect[2] }, { "close" },
        }) or ring(x, y, s.circle)
        local brush = gfx.solid(k == "sensor" and C.muted or C.accent)
        table.insert(marks, gfx.stroke({
          path = path, brush = brush, width = 1.5, dashes = k == "sensor" and { 6, 4 } or nil,
        }))
      end
    end
  end
  return marks
end

-- A ring at every socket the dragged plug fits, filled where it would snap.
local function socket_marks()
  local marks = {}
  for _, s in ipairs(drag and drag.sockets or {}) do
    local circle = ring(s.x, s.y, 9)
    local on = drag.snap and drag.snap.to == s.to and drag.snap.socket == s.socket
    local brush = gfx.solid(on and C.accent or C.muted)
    table.insert(marks, on and gfx.fill({ path = circle, brush = brush })
      or gfx.stroke({ path = circle, brush = brush, width = 2 }))
  end
  return marks
end

-- Clip handles are made once per press of play, so each press starts every clip from its top.
local function start(entities)
  play = { name = M.name, clips = {} }
  for _, e in ipairs(entities) do
    local r = rest(e.asset)
    local clip = e.clip and r and r.asset.clips and r.asset.clips[e.clip]
    if clip then
      play.clips[e.id] = gfx.clip(clip)
    end
  end
end

-- One world entity. A mounted one rides its socket's part with `turn`, pivoting on its own plug,
-- so a hat nods with the head; the world carries only by an entity that is not itself carried.
local function world_entity(e, by_id, at)
  local r = look(e)
  if not r or not at[e.id] then
    return false
  end
  local out = { id = e.id, pos = at[e.id], drawing = r.drawing, clip = play.clips[e.id] }
  local host = e.mount and by_id[e.mount.to]
  local h = host and not host.mount and rest(host.asset)
  local socket = h and h.asset.sockets and h.asset.sockets[e.mount.socket]
  local plug = r.asset.plug
  if socket and plug then
    out.attach = { to = host.id, part = socket.part, at = socket.at, pivot = plug.at, turn = true }
  end
  for k, v in pairs(S.fields(e, r.asset)) do
    out[k] = v
  end
  return out
end

-- Stage play: the scene as a world, at drawing scale — the viewport's zoom does the rest.
local function world(scene)
  local at, by_id = placements(scene.entities), {}
  for _, e in ipairs(scene.entities) do
    by_id[e.id] = e
  end
  local w, h = scene.size[1], scene.size[2]
  -- Entities are the world's own positional entries: a nested list would read as one entity.
  local spec = { id = "stage-play", width = w, height = h, fill = C.floor }
  for i, e in ipairs(scene.entities) do
    spec[i] = world_entity(e, by_id, at)
  end
  return ui.world(spec)
end

-- "edit" and "play" for a stage, made with the editor's own chip.
function S.bar(chip)
  local playing = play ~= nil and play.name == M.name
  local scene = M.asset.scene
  return ui.row({
    gap = 6,
    chip("stage:edit", "edit", not playing, function()
      play = nil
    end),
    chip("stage:play", "play", playing, function()
      if scene then
        start(scene.entities)
      end
    end),
  })
end

function S.view()
  local scene = M.asset.scene
  if not scene then
    return ui.text({ "opening the stage…", color = C.muted, no_wrap = true })
  end
  if play and play.name == M.name then
    return world(scene)
  end
  local w, h = scene.size[1], scene.size[2]
  last = placements(scene.entities)
  local items = { backdrop(w, h) }
  for _, e in ipairs(scene.entities) do
    local r, p = look(e), last[e.id]
    if r and p then
      local place = { 1, 0, 0, 1, p[1], p[2] }
      table.insert(items, gfx.instance({ id = e.id, visual = r.frame, transform = place }))
    end
  end
  for _, mark in ipairs(body_marks(scene.entities)) do
    table.insert(items, mark)
  end
  for _, mark in ipairs(socket_marks()) do
    table.insert(items, mark)
  end
  return ui.frame({
    id = "stage-canvas",
    visual = gfx.frame({ width = w, height = h, table.unpack(items) }),
    on_drag = function(e)
      on_drag(e, scene.entities)
    end,
  })
end

-- The scene's entities, for the side panel: id, the asset it shows, and what it is mounted on.
function S.rows()
  local scene = M.asset.scene
  local rows = {}
  for _, e in ipairs(scene and scene.entities or {}) do
    local where = e.mount and ("on " .. e.mount.to .. "." .. e.mount.socket) or e.asset
    table.insert(rows, { id = e.id, note = where })
  end
  return rows
end

return S

-- The selected part's fields as inputs. A field holds a draft while you type; Enter checks it and
-- writes once, Esc drops it. A value that doesn't parse turns the field red and writes nothing,
-- so the drawing never sees it.
local C = require("theme")
local M = require("model")

local I = { rev = 0 } -- bumped by every write: the canvas rebuilds from the patched mirror

local drafts = {} -- field id -> the text being typed
local showing = nil -- whose fields `drafts` belongs to

local function number(s)
  return tonumber(s)
end

local function positive(s)
  local n = tonumber(s)
  return n and n > 0 and n or nil
end

-- What the asset's var `name` holds: "colour", "number", or nil when it has no such var.
local function var_kind(name)
  local v = M.asset.vars and M.asset.vars[name]
  return type(v) == "string" and "colour" or type(v) == "number" and "number" or nil
end

local function plain_colour(s)
  return pcall(gfx.solid, s) and s or nil
end

-- A colour field takes a colour or `@name` of a colour var; typing a colour unlinks the shape.
local function colour(s)
  local name = s:match("^@(.+)$")
  if name then
    return var_kind(name) == "colour" and s or nil
  end
  return plain_colour(s)
end

-- A width takes a positive number or `@name` of a number var.
local function length(s)
  local name = s:match("^@(.+)$")
  if name then
    return var_kind(name) == "number" and s or nil
  end
  return positive(s)
end

-- A small square of the colour a value shows: a var's, when it names one.
local function swatch(v)
  local name = type(v) == "string" and v:match("^@(.+)$")
  local c = name and M.asset.vars and M.asset.vars[name] or v
  local ok = type(c) == "string" and plain_colour(c)
  return ui.row({ w = 14, h = 14, no_shrink = true, radius = 3, fill = ok and c or C.canvas,
    stroke = { 1, C.muted } })
end

-- `base` extended by more segments: a new table, so the base can be shared.
local function at(base, ...)
  local out = table.clone(base)
  for _, seg in ipairs({ ... }) do
    table.insert(out, seg)
  end
  return out
end

-- `lead` (optional) sits between the label and the input: a colour's swatch.
local function field(id, label, value, parse, path, lead)
  local text = drafts[id] or tostring(value)
  local bad = drafts[id] ~= nil and parse(drafts[id]) == nil
  local function commit()
    local v = drafts[id] and parse(drafts[id])
    if v ~= nil then
      M.asset:set(path, v)
      drafts[id] = nil
      I.rev += 1
    end
  end
  return ui.row({
    gap = 6,
    align_center = true,
    ui.row({ w = 72, ui.text({ label, color = C.muted, font_size = 11, no_wrap = true }) }),
    lead or false,
    ui.input({
      id = id,
      value = text,
      grow = true,
      h = 26,
      px = 8,
      radius = 4,
      fill = C.canvas,
      stroke = { 1, bad and C.bad or C.row_selected },
      color = bad and C.bad or C.text,
      font_size = 12,
      on_input = function(v)
        drafts[id] = v
      end,
      on_enter = commit,
      on_esc = function()
        drafts[id] = nil
      end,
    }),
  })
end

local function note(label, text)
  return ui.row({
    gap = 6,
    ui.row({ w = 72, ui.text({ label, color = C.muted, font_size = 11, no_wrap = true }) }),
    ui.text({ text, color = C.muted, font_size = 12, no_wrap = true }),
  })
end

-- One shape's fields: a gradient fill is shown but not edited yet; a missing stroke isn't offered.
local function shape_fields(base, i, s, out)
  local id = "field:" .. base[4] .. ":" .. i .. ":"
  local here = at(base, "shapes", i)
  table.insert(out, ui.text({ "shape " .. i, color = C.text, font_size = 12, mt = 6, no_wrap = true }))
  if s.shadow then
    local sh = at(here, "shadow")
    table.insert(out, field(id .. "blur", "blur", s.shadow.blur, length, at(sh, "blur")))
    table.insert(out, field(id .. "color", "colour", s.shadow.color, colour, at(sh, "color"), swatch(s.shadow.color)))
    return
  end
  if type(s.fill) == "string" then
    table.insert(out, field(id .. "fill", "fill", s.fill, colour, at(here, "fill"), swatch(s.fill)))
  elseif s.fill then

  for name in pairs(vars or {}) do

  end
  table.sort(names)
  local out = { ui.text({ "vars", color = C.accent, font_size = 13, mt = 12, no_wrap = true }) }
  for _, name in ipairs(names) do
    local v = vars[name]
    local is_colour = type(v) == "string"
    local parse = is_colour and plain_colour or positive
    local lead = is_colour and swatch(v) or nil
    table.insert(out, field("var:" .. name, name, v, parse, { "vars", name }, lead))
  end
  return out
end

-- The fields of part `p`, or nothing for no part.
function I.view(p)
  local who = p and M.name .. ":" .. p.id
  if who ~= showing then -- drafts belong to the part they were typed for
    showing, drafts = who, {}
  end
  if not p then
    return {}
  end
  local base = { "views", M.view, "parts", p.id }
  local id = "field:" .. p.id .. ":pivot:"
  local out = { ui.text({ p.id, color = C.accent, font_size = 13, mt = 12, no_wrap = true }) }
  table.insert(out, field(id .. "x", "pivot x", p.pivot[1], number, at(base, "pivot", 1)))
  table.insert(out, field(id .. "y", "pivot y", p.pivot[2], number, at(base, "pivot", 2)))
  for i, s in ipairs(p.shapes or {}) do
    shape_fields(base, i, s, out)
  end
  return out
end

return I

local C = require("theme")

-- The selected part's path points as canvas dots. Each dot is its own part, so a press on it
-- names it: `pt:<shape>:<command>:<k>`, k counting the command's points — its last is the end
-- point (filled), any before it curve controls (hollow, tied to their end by a guide line).
local H = {}

-- Sizes are on screen: `s`, the viewport's zoom, divides them out so they never grow with it.
local R = 4 -- a dot's radius
local GRAB = 10 -- how near a press must land to take it: a hand is not as exact as the dot

local function circle(x, y, r)
  local k = r * 0.5523 -- a circle's cubic handle length
  return {
    { "move", x + r, y },
    { "cubic", x + r, y + k, x + k, y + r, x, y + r },
    { "cubic", x - k, y + r, x - r, y + k, x - r, y },
    { "cubic", x - r, y - k, x - k, y - r, x, y - r },
    { "cubic", x + k, y - r, x + r, y - k, x + r, y },
    { "close" },
  }
end

local function dot(id, x, y, control, s)
  local fill = control and C.canvas or C.accent
  local ring = control and C.accent or C.canvas
  local shapes = {
    { path = circle(x, y, GRAB / s), fill = "#00000000" }, -- unseen, but the part's to hit
    { path = circle(x, y, R / s), fill = fill, stroke = { 1.5 / s, ring } },
  }
  return { id = id, pivot = { x, y }, shapes = shapes }
end

-- A curve's first control leans on where the curve starts; every later one, on where it ends.
local function guide(lines, from, to, s)
  local path = { { "move", from[1], from[2] }, { "line", to[1], to[2] } }
  table.insert(lines, { path = path, stroke = { 1 / s, C.accent } })
end

-- Parts to append to the canvas drawing for `part`, at canvas scale `z`, seen at zoom `s`.
function H.parts(part, z, s)
  local lines, controls, ends = {}, {}, {}
  for i, shape in ipairs(part.shapes or {}) do
    local last = nil -- the previous command's end: this one's start
    for j, cmd in ipairs(shape.path or {}) do -- a shadow has no path
      local pts = {}
      for k = 2, #cmd - 1, 2 do
        table.insert(pts, { cmd[k] * z, cmd[k + 1] * z })
      end
      local stop = pts[#pts]
      for k, p in ipairs(pts) do
        if k < #pts then
          guide(lines, k == 1 and last or stop, p, s)
        end
        local control = k < #pts
        local d = dot("pt:" .. i .. ":" .. j .. ":" .. k, p[1], p[2], control, s)
        table.insert(control and controls or ends, d)
      end
      last = stop or last
    end
  end
  -- The guides go first, under the dots; a press on one is no point. Ends go last, over every
  -- control: at 1× a cubic's end sits 3 units from its controls, and the top dot takes a press.
  local out = #lines > 0 and { { id = "pt:guides", pivot = { 0, 0 }, shapes = lines } } or {}
  for _, d in ipairs(controls) do
    table.insert(out, d)
  end
  for _, d in ipairs(ends) do
    table.insert(out, d)
  end
  return out
end

-- The controls that ride with point `k` of command `j`, so a curve keeps its shape as its end
-- moves: the cubic's control into it and the next cubic's out of it. A quad's one control
-- belongs to both its ends, so it stays; a control moves alone.
function H.riders(path, j, k)
  local cmd, after, out = path[j], path[j + 1], {}
  if k < (#cmd - 1) / 2 then
    return out
  end
  if cmd[1] == "cubic" then
    table.insert(out, { j = j, k = 2 })
  end
  if after and after[1] == "cubic" then
    table.insert(out, { j = j + 1, k = 1 })
  end
  return out
end

return H

-- Siege: a side-on gravity world with a chain of causes. A slingshot fires a stone (dotted arc
-- previews the shot under the world's gravity) at a castle of stone, wood and glass; the collapse
-- topples a run of dominoes, the last pushes a marble down a ramp into a bucket that lights up.
-- Pigs score when they fall to the ground. Also a toy: a swinging wrecking ball on a chain
-- (rope joints), a seesaw (pin joint), bomb (`blast`), moon/flip gravity, a gravity well, and any
-- loose body can be dragged and thrown (`grab` / `release`). Nothing runs per frame: Lua
-- describes bodies and hears zones; Rapier does the moving. Lua cannot read a body's position, so
-- nothing here depends on one.
local W, H, FY = 960, 520, 480 -- the world, and the floor's top
local C = {
  bg = "#0b0d16", panel = "#1a1e2e", text = "#e8ebf5", muted = "#8f96b0", accent = "#ffd166",
  button = "#2a3050", button_hover = "#3a4270", lit = "#ffe066",
}
local G_NORMAL, G_MOON, G_FLIP = { 0, 900 }, { 0, 280 }, { 0, -900 }

-- ── drawing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function rectp(x, y, w, h)
  return { { "move", x, y }, { "line", x + w, y }, { "line", x + w, y + h }, { "line", x, y + h }, { "close" } }
end
local function disc(cx, cy, r)
  local k = r * 0.5523
  return { { "move", cx, cy - r }, { "cubic", cx + k, cy - r, cx + r, cy - k, cx + r, cy },
    { "cubic", cx + r, cy + k, cx + k, cy + r, cx, cy + r }, { "cubic", cx - k, cy + r, cx - r, cy + k, cx - r, cy },
    { "cubic", cx - r, cy - k, cx - k, cy - r, cx, cy - r }, { "close" } }
end
local function ellipse(cx, cy, rx, ry)
  local kx, ky = rx * 0.5523, ry * 0.5523
  return { { "move", cx, cy - ry }, { "cubic", cx + kx, cy - ry, cx + rx, cy - ky, cx + rx, cy },
    { "cubic", cx + rx, cy + ky, cx + kx, cy + ry, cx, cy + ry }, { "cubic", cx - kx, cy + ry, cx - rx, cy + ky, cx - rx, cy },
    { "cubic", cx - rx, cy - ky, cx - kx, cy - ry, cx, cy - ry }, { "close" } }
end
local function drawing(w, h, shapes)
  return gfx.drawing({ size = { w, h }, parts = { { id = "it", pivot = { w / 2, h / 2 }, shapes = shapes } } })
end
local cache = {}
local function memo(key, make)
  if not cache[key] then cache[key] = make() end
  return cache[key]
end

-- Interpolates two #rrggbb colours: stacked bands make a gradient, since a drawing's fill is solid.
local function mix(a, b, t)
  local function ch(s, i) return tonumber(s:sub(i, i + 1), 16) end
  local out = "#"
  for i = 2, 6, 2 do out = out .. string.format("%02x", math.floor(ch(a, i) + (ch(b, i) - ch(a, i)) * t + 0.5)) end
  return out
end
local function bands(x, y, w, h, stops, n)
  local shapes = {}
  for i = 0, n - 1 do
    local t = i / (n - 1) * (#stops - 1)
    local s = math.min(#stops - 2, math.floor(t))
    shapes[#shapes + 1] = { path = rectp(x, y + h * i / n, w, h / n + 1), fill = mix(stops[s + 1], stops[s + 2], t - s) }
  end
  return shapes
end

local function sky()
  return memo("sky", function()
    local s = bands(0, 0, W, FY, { "#0e1432", "#2c2457", "#7a3a6e", "#e0667a", "#ffb56b" }, 30)
    for i = 1, 40 do -- stars, thinning toward the horizon
      local x, y = (i * 137) % W, (i * 71) % 200
      s[#s + 1] = { path = disc(x, y, 0.8 + (i % 3) * 0.4), fill = "#ffffff" .. (i % 2 == 0 and "cc" or "77") }
    end
    s[#s + 1] = { path = disc(780, 90, 34), fill = "#fff1c9" }
    s[#s + 1] = { path = disc(792, 84, 30), fill = "#ffe29a44" }
    -- far hills
    s[#s + 1] = { path = { { "move", 0, FY }, { "line", 0, 380 }, { "quad", 140, 330, 260, 372 }, { "quad", 380, 410, 520, 360 },
      { "quad", 660, 310, 800, 372 }, { "quad", 900, 410, W, 380 }, { "line", W, FY }, { "close" } }, fill = "#3b2a5acc" }
    s[#s + 1] = { path = { { "move", 0, FY }, { "line", 0, 430 }, { "quad", 200, 390, 360, 440 }, { "quad", 560, 480, 700, 430 },
      { "quad", 840, 390, W, 440 }, { "line", W, FY }, { "close" } }, fill = "#2a1f45" }
    return drawing(W, FY, s)
  end)
end

local function ground()
  return memo("ground", function()
    local s = bands(0, 0, W, H - FY, { "#4a7a3a", "#2f5a2c", "#2a2018", "#18120d" }, 14)
    s[#s + 1] = { path = rectp(0, 0, W, 3), fill = "#8fd45a" }
    return drawing(W, H - FY, s)
  end)
end

-- A lit block: body, bright top edge, dark bottom edge, outline.
local function slab(w, h, base, hi, lo, edge)
  return memo(table.concat({ "slab", w, h, base }, ":"), function()
    return drawing(w, h, {
      { path = rectp(0, 0, w, h), fill = base }, { path = rectp(0, 0, w, math.min(3, h / 3)), fill = hi },
      { path = rectp(0, h - math.min(3, h / 3), w, math.min(3, h / 3)), fill = lo },
      { path = rectp(0.5, 0.5, w - 1, h - 1), stroke = { 1, edge or "#00000066" } },
    })
  end)
end
local function ball(r, base, hi, lo, mark)
  return memo(table.concat({ "ball", r, base }, ":"), function()
    local s = { { path = disc(r, r, r), fill = lo }, { path = disc(r - 1, r - 1, r - 2), fill = base },
      { path = disc(r * 0.7, r * 0.65, r * 0.38), fill = hi } }
    if mark then s[#s + 1] = { path = rectp(r - 1.5, 2, 3, r * 0.6), fill = mark } end
    s[#s + 1] = { path = disc(r, r, r - 0.5), stroke = { 1, "#00000077" } }
    return drawing(2 * r, 2 * r, s)
  end)
end
local function pig(r)
  return memo("pig" .. r, function()
    local e = r * 0.42
    return drawing(2 * r, 2 * r, {
      { path = disc(r, r, r), fill = "#4f9d3a" }, { path = disc(r - 1, r - 1, r - 2), fill = "#7bd357" },
      { path = disc(r, r * 1.2, r * 0.42), fill = "#5aa840" }, -- snout
      { path = disc(r - 3, r * 1.2, 1.6), fill = "#2d5a1f" }, { path = disc(r + 3, r * 1.2, 1.6), fill = "#2d5a1f" },
      { path = disc(r - e, r * 0.75, 3.2), fill = "#ffffff" }, { path = disc(r + e, r * 0.75, 3.2), fill = "#ffffff" },
      { path = disc(r - e, r * 0.78, 1.5), fill = "#102010" }, { path = disc(r + e, r * 0.78, 1.5), fill = "#102010" },
      { path = disc(r, r, r - 0.5), stroke = { 1, "#1f4a14" } },
    })
  end)
end
local function invisible(w, h)
  return memo("inv" .. w .. "x" .. h, function() return drawing(w, h, { { path = rectp(0, 0, w, h), fill = "#00000000" } }) end)
end

local KIND = { -- how each block is drawn and made
  stone = { base = "#8d93a6", hi = "#c5cad9", lo = "#5b6075", mat = { bounce = 0.05, friction = 0.02, grip = 0.9, density = 3 } },
  wood = { base = "#c58b4e", hi = "#e8b27a", lo = "#8a5a2c", mat = { bounce = 0.3, friction = 0.02, grip = 0.7, density = 0.7 } },
  glass = { base = "#8fe3f8aa", hi = "#ffffffcc", lo = "#4aa7c4aa", edge = "#e8fbffcc",
    mat = { bounce = 0.5, friction = 0.02, grip = 0.4, density = 0.8 } },
  domino = { base = "#e0505a", hi = "#ff9aa0", lo = "#9a2a35", mat = { bounce = 0.2, friction = 0.02, grip = 0.9, density = 1.5 } },
}

-- ── the scene as data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
local gen = 0 -- bumps on reset: fresh ids respawn everything where it began
local function N(name) return gen == 0 and name or (name .. "~" .. gen) end

local function castle()
  local b = {}
  local function add(name, kind, x, y, w, h) b[#b + 1] = { name = name, kind = kind, x = x, y = y, w = w, h = h } end
  for i = 0, 4 do -- two stone pillars of five
    add("sl" .. i, "stone", 440, FY - 28 * (i + 1), 28, 28)
    add("sr" .. i, "stone", 516, FY - 28 * (i + 1), 28, 28)
  end
  add("beam1", "wood", 432, 326, 120, 14)
  add("wl", "wood", 448, 282, 16, 44)
  add("wr", "wood", 524, 282, 16, 44)
  add("beam2", "wood", 432, 270, 120, 12)
  add("g1", "glass", 440, 254, 16, 16)
  add("g2", "glass", 536, 254, 16, 16)
  add("g3", "glass", 466, 300, 10, 26)
  add("g4", "glass", 512, 300, 10, 26)
  -- dominoes grow taller along the run, so each hits harder than the last; the last is a hammer
  local x = 600
  for i, h in ipairs({ 30, 34, 38, 43, 48, 54, 60 }) do
    add("d" .. (i - 1), "domino", x, 440 - h, 8, h)
    x = x + 8 + 0.45 * h
  end
  add("crate1", "wood", 478, FY - 24, 24, 24)
  add("seesaw_c1", "wood", 196, FY - 58, 22, 24)
